pr_title: Improved support for implicit field ids and immutable properties
pr_body:
The option to enable implicit field ids can now be configured both at project and type level, and has been changed to an enum that better communicates what constitutes implicit fields. Note that the GenerateFieldIds enum has been linked from the Abstractions project into the CodeGenerator project, to avoid adding a project dependency.

I've introduced an OrleansConstructorAttribute (inheriting from ActivatorUtilitiesConstructorAttribute) and confirmed that this is still picked up by ActivatorUtilities. The code only sets the "supportPrimaryConstructorParameters" when exactly one constructor is annotated.

Properties mapping to a constructor parameter are now flagged as such (previously this was only done for fields), as this allows the code to not reject properties without an accessible setter. This improves support for immutable classes.

I also found a couple of spelling mistakes and corrected those along the way. There are no unit test regressions.

This fixes #7937, and provides a workaround for #7936.

###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/api/codeflow?pullrequest=https://github.com/dotnet/orleans/pull/7958)

Yes, I agree. Alternatively we could change the code to allow multiple annotations and just pick the first one found (this is how System.Text.Json works, afaik). I'm ok with this, but it's the more error prone option. On the other hand, I don't expect this to impact many users, if any. We can also add an analyzer later, if our intuition turns out to be incorrect.

I'm not used to multi-day delays in correspondences ;), so impatient me just did the analyzer. However, it looks like all of the analyzers call the same AnalyzeTypeDeclaration, so they're not exactly perf optimized. An issue for another day, though.

I've split the field id assignment logic into a helper class and am working on the hash-based assignment logic, should have an updated PR soon.

issue_context.title: Serialization: GenerateFieldIds does not work with immutable types
issue_context.body:
I have been unable to get Orleans to serialize objects, when GenerateFieldIds is enabled, without adding an accessible setter to all properties. Neither a private setter or init-only properties are enough.

Somehow object construction must be different when GenerateFieldIds is enabled, because if I add explicit `[Id]` annotations (and turn off GenerateFieldIds) then I do not need to have the setters.

The ideal solution would be to treat properties that are initialized on the constructor as if they had a setter.

review_comments: I'm a little confused by this logic. If there's an auto-property then we can imply the id based on the position of a matching constructor parameter, but not if it's a regular field (no matching property). Conversely, the corresponding property member will not have the same id because the logic for `IPropertySymbol` above only checks for an `Id` attribute. Am I missing something?

This logic is carried over from the original bits (i.e. how it used to work), but it also confuses me a bit. I think the idea is that fields are more important than properties, so properties are only included if they are explicitly `Id`-annotated, whereas for fields it attempts to first find the corresponding property, and if that fails, attempts to map to a ctor parameter index. The FieldIdAssignmentHelper doesn't know that the code generator prefers fields over properties, it just has logic to attempt to find an id for each member.

Let me know if you want the logic to also check for constructor parameters for properties.. but given how the code generator currently works, I don't think it'd ever get used.
